utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-82-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ljube Boskoski and Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. First of all, I would like to welcome everybody to the Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: -- the defendants are unable to understand the proceedings in their own language or at least a language which they understand. Mr. Boskoski, everything okay?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOSKOSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Mr. Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TARCULOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now appearances for the accused. From Mr. Boskoski who is representing --

utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. For Mr. Ljube Boskoski, for the accused Boskoski, attorney Dragan Godzo from Ohrid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Mr. Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the accused Mr. Johan Tarculovski, Your Honour, Antonio Apostolski, attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, Bill Smith for the Prosecution with Anees Ahmed as trial attorney and Salla Moilanen as case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, perhaps, before we come to the issues I would like to explain why we have come together in a public meeting so the public should know what the purpose of this meeting is. The initial appearances were held on the 1th of April, 2005 for Mr. Boskoski and the 18th of April for Mr. Tarculovski, and the Trial Chamber is the required person to Rule 65 bis to hold a Status Conference within 120 days after the initial appearance. That would be the case now. To organise exchanges between the parties as to ensure expeditious preparation for trial and to allow the accused to raise issues in relation to his mental and physical condition. In preparation of the Status Conference, a Rule 65 ter Conference took place yesterday, August 18. I have been fully briefed about the discussions that have taken place during that conference, so you may be aware that I have read the transcript and so we don't have to repeat everything what has been discussed between the parties and Mr. Von Hebel yesterday. The first point I would like to address are outstanding motions. With regard to Mr. Boskoski, you brought in a Defence challenge to the form of the indictment. You have already been told that this -- the decision of the Trial Chamber is almost finished. As of now, I think it will be issued on Monday. So there is nothing to be done in this respect so far. We have another motion, both by Mr. Boskoski and Mr. Tarculovski, for further protective measures. As you may be aware, the decision was issued on August 17, so it should be at your disposal in the meantime. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I still have not received the decision. Since the 16th of August, I am travelling, and in my locker where I receive my mail it has not been distributed still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Godzo -- Mr. Apostolski. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have not received this decision as well, possibly because I was travelling since the 16th. I'm here in The Hague and this is why we have not the confirmation that it has been received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Was it received by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We received it late yesterday. We can provide our friends with a copy after the hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Anyway, it should be on the way. If it's not yet in your lockers, perhaps you will find it when you get back. The next issues we have to deal with are the issues of disclosure. One has to do with Rule 66(A)(i). Pursuant to this rule the Prosecution has already made available to the Defence for both accused in a language both accused understand copies of all the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought. This was done on the 2nd of May, 2005. I think this point has been discussed in the 65 ter Conference yesterday. So from my point of view there is no need for further discussion in this respect. Is that the case? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you. I saw some nodding from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. No objection. We are fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, with regard to Rule 66(A)(ii) which deals with witness statements which have to be made -- have to be disclosed by the Prosecution before -- in a certain time before the trial starts. At this point we have been informed that we already deliberated with regard to length of the trial, and I have been made aware of the various problems, practical problems, you see. So from -- at this point of time, I would not like to make a fixed -- give a fixed date, because this date for the start of the trial is also somehow important for the time of disclosure. So at this point the Trial Chamber will not fix a completion date for Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosure, but, and I would like to make this very clear, but imposes on the Prosecution an obligation to all resources available in as speedy as possible completion of the disclosure under this provision in light of the need to prepare for trial at the earliest possible moment. Now we come to Rule -- disclosure with regard to Rule 68. And perhaps to explain it to the public, Rule 68 is quite important for the Defence, because there is an obligation on the Prosecution to make the Defence aware of the material which may be of exculpatory or mitigating character, and for this reason the Defence should be in a position to take notice of this early enough to use it for their clients. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Again here we have the problem that a disclosure date depends on the beginning of the trial, and since we at this point we do not have a date fixed yet, I would only say more or less the same what I already told I with regard to 66(A)(ii). At this point the Trial Chamber will not fix a completion date for Rule 68 disclosure but imposes on the Prosecution the obligation to put all resources available in as speedy as possible completion of the disclosure under this provision in light of the need to prepare for trial at the earliest possible moment. Now, are there any other matters which either party wants to raise on the subject of disclosure apart from what has already been discussed at this Rule 65 ter Conference? So what I mean is everything what you have already told yesterday in the meeting does not need to be repeated here, only if there are any new aspects which might be brought to the awareness of the Trial Chamber. I see no need for this. Then I may perhaps address the tentative trial schedule. You will remember that yesterday the Senior Legal Officer presented to you the hope or the desire of the Court to start with the trial as speedy -- as soon as possible. Now, you have been made aware, there are -- at this moment there are still too many uncertain and at present unknown factors to allow for proper scheduling. For this reason, we will not put a fixed date on you. However, it is not to be excluded that this case will have to start at trial at some point at the end of the year. The Court is very much aware of all the work that still needs to be done to make the case ready for trial. Nevertheless, I am not convinced that a trial by the end of the year would not be feasible at all. Therefore, the Pre-Trial Judge want to make it clear in order to both parties now without specific deadlines that a maximum of resources have to be put to this case in order to proceed with the highest expediency possible. I would like to give you a reason. The accused are entitled to a fair trial within a reasonable time. The parties owe it to the accused who are in the pre-trial detention to make use of any opportunity that may arise to get the case started in trial as soon as reasonably possible. And perhaps to explain it to you once more, as you have been made aware there might be a chance to start the trial at the end of November or the beginning of December. Now, if this time is missed, the alternative is not that you may start in March or April. The alternative may be that if this point is missed that the trial may start to a much later date. That's the problem, because there are quite some changes. So it's not -- it's certain that there may be a possibility to start a new trial at the end of November, beginning of December, and you have also been informed that because of some arrangements in the courtrooms and so on that the beginning of the trial would not be a very speedy step, but what would be necessary is to start. And for this reason, I really would like to urge you to go to work, so to say, as soon as possible or even to put a lot of emphasis in it. Now, as soon as a better picture emerges from the various factors that are yet uncertain and unknown, there may be a need for a new Rule 65 ter Conference and a Status Conference in order to further discuss with the parties how to prepare this case for an early as possible start. So I hope it has become clear what our intention is. Not the least with regard to the accused we would like to start as soon as possible and try to -- not to miss a chance if it is -- will be presented or maybe available at the end of the year. Are there any further comments? That seems not to be the case or --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just a couple of brief comments. Your Honour, the Prosecution gives Your Honour the utmost assurances that it will be working as fast as it can to ensure a fair and expeditious trial for the two accused. Obviously the concerns raised yesterday was in relation to the fairness of the trial and the amount of time for disclosure and translation. However, on Your Honour's point about if it was such the case that the trial may possibly start, say, late November, early December, we discussed with the Senior Legal Officer some possibilities of using the Rule 71 procedure of taking perhaps depositions for those few days that are available and still the Trial Chamber or the legal officer receiving evidence which would not in fact delay the trial in substance at all; however, the possibility of being able to provide the pre-trial brief and other exhibits and witness summaries at some date closer towards when the trial can start in earnest, perhaps -- apparently about five days a week. I would strongly ask that be considered in this instance, and that may be able to achieve the serious concerns the Prosecution have about the fairness of the trial if it starts -- if it does start very quickly, and obviously the even more serious concerns raised by the Defence in relation to their ability to prepare for trial. It would be creative and obviously the Prosecution are always looking for ways in which we can expedite these matters and -- but I think it would possibly -- a possible solution that would alleviate the problems for all parties if that was to come about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Any comments from your side to this or would you join what has been said by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Regarding the time needed before the -- before scheduling the start of the trial and the time that Defence needs to prepare for the trial, yesterday at the conference, 65 ter, I have presented my position that the time needed to prepare the defence will be longer than the -- will take longer than the date you presented, and that too early start of the trial can have consequences to the right of the accused to have a fair trial since objectively we need more time to prepare for the defence. And I confirm that there is an excellent cooperation with the Prosecutor's party. We have been submitted all the necessary materials supporting the indictment, but objectively the Defence needs more time to be able to study them, analyse them, and Defence also needs to prepare its evidence for the trial. Due to these reason, we maintain that the time we needed to prepare for the trial is as we expressed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So what we will do is that we take into consideration what has been proposed by the Prosecution with regard to Rule 71, and we will also take into consideration what has been proposed from your side, and as soon as there is a new situation, when we have clearer indications Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. about the situation of the court in general, we will come back to this. Now, are there any other matters the parties want to address? If this is not the case, I would like to ask the defendants whether they have anything to bring in with regard to their state of health or the condition of detention. Mr. Boskoski, would you like to -- on your behalf your Defence counsel to say?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOSKOSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I respect my Defence counsel. I respect this Court. I respect the Prosecutor's office. I have proven it in the past four years of my intense cooperation with the Tribunal. But I think that regarding my health status, I myself can only answer and the competent doctors possibly. But for the moment I can say that I don't have any health problems, except that I'm -- I'm for a year already been submitted to a psychological torture which started with the Rastanski Lozja staged case and culminated with the acquittal in the first instance, and this torture is reflected also throughout my stay here. That is a psychological torture on me, on my family, against my family, and against my Macedonia. So from this viewpoint, since health is a broad notion, I think that regarding the psychological component of it, I feel constant pressure due to a single reason. Not only am I guilty [as interpreted], Your Honour, but I'm now shocked from the statements that already some trial is being scheduled. I continue to believe that there is not a single element to start a trial. Not only I believe it. We have sufficient evidence to support it. And in the recent days I by accident stumbled on documents that shocked me. And we will submit them in the forthcoming period. There has been a confusion regarding the dates. My cooperation as a minister of foreign affairs with the distinguished Madam Carla Del Ponte started on the 20th of November, 2001, which means two months after the events in Ljuboten. The Tribunal has already been in Macedonia and by the government's decision and in agreement with the Tribunal we have intensified the cooperation and we started discovering the crimes perpetrated in Macedonia, and this is why I'm shocked when I'm reading that instead of the date 20th of November and instead of the dates in 2001 they are transferred into 2002, and certainly the Prosecutor's office has been misled when they say that our cooperation started. The case has been taken in -- deferred in May 2002 while Ljuboten case has been deferred in -- or opened in January 2002, two months after the Ljuboten offence when there has been no post-mortem, no exhumation. The bodies of the killed people in Ljuboten have been -- not been found, and I regret loss of their lives, as I will loss of any life. These are my objections. I made a connection between my health problems and this part which creates for me a special agitation when I hear that as early as Monday and that the start of the trial date is being discussed, a process that should take place before this Court. I think that absolutely I am innocent and there is no need of any process, and we will be able to convince the Prosecutor's office soon having in mind the Defence material that -- Defence evidence we have which is indisputable and firm. Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Mr. Boskoski --

utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: May I speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I want you to make you aware of the problems of this. I didn't want to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: Excuse me. I ask you for permission to speak. I noticed one mistake in the record. In the second paragraph of the accused statement it is -- it was written -- that is one mistake. It is not "I am not guilty," Your Honour. It is written the opposite, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Which line is it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: I don't have on my screen now so I cannot tell you. But it is second paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Can you just make sure that will be corrected. Can you give me the line? I don't have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: It's not on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Is it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: It's not at this moment on my screen because it has --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Its align 9:22.

utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: Can you change it? I think it misses one crucial -- yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Line 22. Yes, of course it will be corrected. Thank you very much. Mr. Tarculovski, would you like to say something with regard to your -- with regard to your health and the condition of the detention? So that's not the place to make please this or that way, go that direction.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: His microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Would you please repeat. We didn't hear what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry but I cannot hear the defendant. Your Honour, I can't hear the defendant.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Now it is better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: That's better.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TARCULOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to say that my health condition is all right and that I have no comments on the conditions in the detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I -- the Trial Chamber wishes to advise both of the accused that Rule 85 of the Rules of Detention provide a complaint procedure which may be used to raise issues that occur while in detention. So I just wanted to make you aware of these rights. There seems to be no other issue to be raised now. That means the Court now stands adjourned. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: at 2.45 p.m.
